math.title: Chapter 6 Practice Test
math.coverage: 27 questions from all six Chapter 6 lessons: tiling, counting unit squares, multiplying, composite figures (including a missing side length), splitting a side, and area problems.
math.instructions: Answer each question. You can go back before you finish. There are no hints during the test. You will see your score, each lesson's part, and the answers at the end.
math.note: A Study Scoop review of the whole chapter. It is not a teacher test. The class test on Tuesday, Nov 3 is a vocabulary test on Area, Square Unit and Multiply (see the Math Vocabulary Practice Test).

items.prompt: Each tile is 1 unit square. Count the tiles. What is the area in square units?
items.yes: Yes! 30 tiles cover it, so the area is 30 square units.
items.explain: 5 rows of 6 unit squares: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 30 square units.

items.prompt: Which figure is tiled correctly to find its area?

options.why: Figure A has squares lying on top of others.

items.explain: A correct tiling has no gaps and no overlaps: Figure B.

items.prompt: How many more unit squares are needed to cover the whole shape with no gaps?
items.yes: Yes! 7 more unit squares finish the tiling.
items.explain: The shape needs 15 unit squares; 8 are there, so 7 more.

items.prompt: Why must there be no gaps when you tile a shape?

options.text: Space in a gap is not counted.

options.why: The shape does not change; the gaps are simply not counted.
A gap leaves part of the inside uncounted.

items.explain: A gap is inside the shape but not covered, so the count is too small.

items.prompt: What is the area of the shaded shape in square units?
items.explain: 4 + 4 + 2 + 2 = 12 square units.

items.prompt: Each square is 1 square centimeter. What is the area in square centimeters?
items.explain: 4 rows of 5 make 20 square centimeters.

items.prompt: Squares 1 foot on each side cover a mat. 14 of them fit. What is the area of the mat?

options.why: Feet measure a side. Area is in square feet.
The squares are 1 foot on each side.

items.explain: Each square is 1 square foot, so 14 square feet.

items.prompt: Which rectangle has an area of 18 square units?

options.why: Figure B has 4 rows of 4: 16 squares.
Figure C has 2 rows of 8: 16 squares.

items.explain: Figure A: 3 rows of 6 make 18.

items.prompt: This rectangle is 7 centimeters long and 4 centimeters wide. What is its area in square centimeters?
items.explain: 7 × 4 = 28 square centimeters.

items.prompt: This rectangle is 9 feet long and 6 feet wide. What is its area in square feet?
items.explain: 9 × 6 = 54 square feet.

items.prompt: A square tile is 9 inches on each side. What is its area in square inches?
items.explain: 9 × 9 = 81 square inches.

items.prompt: Which equation finds the area of a rectangle 8 meters long and 7 meters wide?

options.why: Adding the sides does not find area.
That adds the sides all the way around.

items.explain: 8 × 7 = 56 square meters.

items.prompt: A rectangle has an area of 24 square feet. Which could be its sides?
What is the area of the figure in square feet?
One side of this figure is marked with a ?. Find that side first. What is the area of the figure in square centimeters?
items.explain: The missing side is 8 - 3 = 5 cm. Split the figure: 3 × 6 = 18 and 5 × 2 = 10. 18 + 10 = 28 square centimeters.

items.prompt: Which two rectangles make this figure, with no overlap?

options.why: The figure is not a 6 by 6 square.
The 2 by 6 part would overlap the top part.

items.explain: Top: 6 by 2 makes 12. Below: 2 by 4 makes 8. 12 + 8 = 20 square inches.

items.prompt: A composite figure covers 50 square meters. One part covers 32 square meters. What does the other part cover?
items.explain: 50 - 32 = 18 square meters.

items.prompt: Use the split picture. Break 16 into 10 + 6, then finish the equations to find the area in square centimeters.
items.explain: 4 × 16 = 4 × 10 + 4 × 6 = 40 + 24 = 64 square centimeters.

items.prompt: The rectangle is 6 by 7. Which matches the split picture?

options.why: 5 + 3 is 8, not 7.
Multiply each part.

items.explain: 30 + 12 = 42 square units.

items.prompt: A rug is 13 feet long and 6 feet wide. Break 13 into 10 + 3. What is its area in square feet?
A student wrote 5 × 14 = (5 × 10) + (4 × 4). What went wrong?

options.text: The second part must keep the 5: 5 × 4.

options.why: Area is multiplied.

items.prompt: Which find the area of the picture? Choose all that are right.

options.why: Adding does not find area.

items.prompt: A school storage room has this floor. One side is marked with a ?. How many square meters of flooring cover the room?
items.explain: The missing side is 9 - 3 = 6 m. Top part: 4 × 6 = 24. Bottom part: 9 × 3 = 27. 24 + 27 = 51 square meters.

items.prompt: Garden A is 6 m by 5 m. Garden B is 8 m by 4 m. Which has the greater area?

options.why: 6 × 5 = 30 is less than 8 × 4 = 32.
30 and 32 are not the same.

items.explain: A: 30 square meters. B: 32 square meters.

items.prompt: A paper letter T has this shape. How many square inches of paper does it use?
items.explain: 6 × 2 = 12 and 2 × 7 = 14. 12 + 14 = 26 square inches.

items.prompt: A poster is 5 feet long and 4 feet wide. It is made 8 feet long. How much more area does it cover?
items.explain: 32 - 20 = 12 square feet more.

items.prompt: A student says a 6 by 4 rug covers 20 square feet because 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20. What is right?

options.why: Adding the sides measures around the rug, not what it covers.
6 + 4 adds two sides.

items.explain: Covering is area: 6 × 4 = 24 square feet.
